__comment: Phase 2 §2.10's infrastructure and application dashboard, with the metric-to-trace link that is the
reason for running all four stores rather than just Prometheus.
EXEMPLARS ARE ENABLED ON THE LATENCY PANEL. An exemplar is a trace id attached to a histogram bucket, so
clicking a latency spike opens a request that was actually slow -- rather than searching traces for the
same time window and hoping. It requires three things to line up, and all three are elsewhere in this
directory: the collector emitting OpenMetrics (enable_open_metrics in otel-gateway.yaml), Prometheus
storing them (--enable-feature=exemplar-storage in docker-compose.yml), and the datasource naming a
trace destination (exemplarTraceIdDestinations in grafana-datasources.yaml). Miss any one and the link
silently does nothing -- there is no error, the dots simply never appear.
title: ForgeOps / Infrastructure and Application Health

panels.title: Telemetry pipeline health -- read this before trusting anything below
Spans shed by the collector
panels.description: Non-zero means memory_limiter is refusing data. That is the collector working as designed -- one that refuses loses only what it refused, one killed by the OOM killer loses everything it held -- but it means the traces and metrics on this page are INCOMPLETE. An empty panel here is the good state; an empty panel because the collector is down looks identical, which is why the panel beside it shows accepted spans.

panels.title: Spans accepted by the collector
panels.description: The companion to the panel on the left. Zero here means nothing is being instrumented or the collector is down; that is a different problem from shedding, and without this panel the two are indistinguishable.

panels.title: Export queue depth
panels.description: Telemetry waiting to leave the collector. A queue that only grows means a downstream store is unreachable, and the queue is bounded -- so past its limit, data is dropped rather than held.

panels.title: Scrape targets up
panels.description: `up` is 1 or 0 per target. A target that has never been scraped is ABSENT rather than 0, which is why this panel shows a count and the table beside it lists names: a count alone cannot distinguish a target that is down from one that was never configured.

panels.title: p95 latency, with exemplars
panels.description: Click a dot to open the trace of a request that was actually that slow. If no dots appear, exemplars are not reaching Prometheus -- see this dashboard's __comment for the three settings that must all be present.

panels.title: 5xx ratio by route
panels.description: Deliberately ABSENT rather than zero where a route had no traffic: the ratio's denominator is the request rate, and rendering 0% for a route nobody called would say 'no errors' about something untested. A gap here means no requests, not no failures.
